reviewHtml:
If their resort 2027 collection was centered on the idea of an Italian summer, Dsquared2’s Dean and Dan Caten went deeper into Italian-ness for their spring 2027. In fact, the duo drew on the Mediterranean folklore of southern Italy, exploring religious symbolism through a spicy lens. Crosses and holy references, along with religious-inspired tattoos, were at the core of this season, with nods to Baz Luhrmann’s Romeo + Juliet. This was especially evident in the gangster-inspired atmosphere, a choice that showcased Dsquared2’s propensity to mix up very different references, often rooted in pop culture.

Shot in a Villa in Lecco, not far from Milan, the portraits of their men’s and women’s proposals immediately highlighted this ritual as a sacred and profane oxymoron. A large cross was applied to a white shirt by exposing the internal pockets usually built into a blazer. Little crosses and small medallions with holy cards were a recurring decoration on jacket lapels and some leather accessories. The theme of purity was further enhanced through doily crochet details on the front pocket of a shirt or on a larger plastron reminiscent of crocheted tablecloths found on church altars, especially in southern Italy. All of these were paired with ripped jeans with a slimmer silhouette, also proposed in a lasered print of typical subjects of classical frescoes.

Men mainly wore the rosary as a necklace; for women, it became an alternative to thin embellishing chains and even jacket fasteners. Lace played a main role as lingerie inserts, like a delicate pink bra as the top part of a sinuous fluorescent green dress, recalling Dsquared2’s tendency to mix components from different garments. The duo applied the same approach to feminine suits with contrasting lingerie applications. Finally, the tropical print with a daggered heart was the duo’s interpretation of the gangster attitude they wanted to use as a pop incursion into this collection.
